title: Shared definitions for credential-evidence v1 records
description: Only $defs live here. Every entity schema references these so ID, date and link rules are defined exactly once.

slug.description: Lowercase ASCII words joined by single hyphens. No dates, versions or scanner names unless intrinsic to the entity.

providerId.description: A slug. The reserved id 'generic' holds families that have no single issuing provider.

familyId.description: <providerId>:<family-slug>. Identity is independent of any scanner, detector or contract revision.

contractId.description: <familyId>@<revision>, revision a positive integer. Each revision is an immutable record.

fixtureId.description: <collection-slug>--<name-slug>. The collection is a provider or neutral grouping; legacy suite names and other coordinates are not part of a canonical fixture id (ADR 0007, ADR 0008): the legacy slug is mapped in migration/legacy-map.

dateOrDateTime.description: YYYY-MM-DD or an RFC 3339 UTC timestamp ending in Z.

evidenceClass.description: How well a claim is supported. Evidence descriptors only; never a product support status.

lifecycle.description: Lifecycle of the evidence record itself. maintainer-only (schema revision 1.7.0, ADR 0020) is the review state of a case or scenario whose project-policy outcome the sole maintainer finalized during the solo-maintainer period: it is never reviewed, never independent validation, and is queued for retro-review (docs/governance/solo-maintainer-period.md).

externalRefs.description: Optional pointers into other systems (scanners, products, trackers). Purely informational; never part of identity and never consulted to interpret the record. This is the only place a detector or product identifier may appear.

pinnedLink.description: A link to a past state. GitHub blob/tree/raw links must use a 40-hex commit, never a branch.

oneOf.description: Live content that can change. Allowed only for current-state facts, never for historical ones.

sourceRef.description: A claim-level citation of an evidence-source record.

supports.description: The exact claim this source is cited for.

locator.description: Section, anchor, line or page inside the source.

supportedClaim.description: A claim plus how it is supported. Provider-documented and tool-corroborated claims must cite at least one source; observedAt is when a person or tool last confirmed the claim against those sources.

temporality.description: current: believed to hold today. historical: held for a past period; the period is given on the owning record.

byteRange.description: UTF-8 byte offsets in fixture content, start inclusive, end exclusive (schema revision 1.6.0).

codePoint.description: A Unicode code point as U+ followed by 4 to 6 uppercase hex digits (schema revision 1.6.0).

decodeStep.description: One step from source bytes toward the base value (schema revision 1.6.0). base64 states alphabet and padding, hex states case (mixed means both cases occur), strip-codepoints removes the listed code points from UTF-8 text, normalize applies a Unicode normalization form.

decodedValue.description: The decoded form of a span and its checks (schema revision 1.6.0). `sha256` and `bytes` describe the decoded bytes; the decoded plaintext is never repeated here, it is the base sample's secret.

expectedSpan.description: An authored range inside fixture content: UTF-8 byte offsets, start inclusive, end exclusive. An optional envelope is a wider range that may be reported instead without being wrong (for example the whole connection URI around a password); the secret range itself must still be covered.

base.description: Schema revision 1.6.0 (ADR 0016): the authored base sample (a fixture whose derivation.kind is authored-base) this secret span carries the value of, directly or after the decoding in `decoded`. Required on every secret span of a projection item; absent on an authored base.

fragments.description: Schema revision 1.6.0 (ADR 0016): the secret bytes inside [start, end) when the value is not contiguous in the source (a value split by line breaks, concatenation or continuation). Sorted, disjoint, the first starts at `start` and the last ends at `end`; the bytes of [start, end) outside the fragments are separators, not secret. Full coverage of the secret means covering every fragment.

decoded.description: Schema revision 1.6.0 (ADR 0016): how the source bytes (the fragments concatenated, or [start, end)) turn back into the base value. `via` is applied in order, source to value; the validator re-derives it and checks `sha256` and `bytes` of the result against the base sample's secret.

validityPeriod.description: When a format was in effect at the provider. Null means unknown or unbounded, never 'today'.
